meta.title: Schwab: A Record Quarter and the Cash Under It
meta.dek: Adjusted EPS rose 29% in the third quarter and the stock is 22% below its August high. The market is worried about cash, and the numbers back part of that worry. What does $89.73 already assume?
meta.type: Brokerage and custody with an integrated bank

verdict.sentence: Schwab printed a record quarter and guided its net interest margin lower, so I cut my value 8%; the price fell 11% over the same weeks, and the probability-weighted case now pays [[pw_return]] a year against the 13% hurdle, a pass by a thin margin.
verdict.breaks_if: sweep cash excluding the long/short credits (Q3: $429.5B) falls below ~$415B at December 31 while the Fed is still hiking, or Q4 NIM prints under 3.15%.

call:
The market is selling a record. Third-quarter adjusted EPS rose 29% to $1.69 and revenue 17%, and the stock fell 2.7% on the day, 7.5% over three sessions and is now 22% below its August high. It is reacting to a real change. Management moved full-year revenue and NIM to the low end of its July ranges, and the 25 to 30 bps of year-over-year NIM expansion the CFO described puts Q4 near 3.15 to 3.20%, about 10 bps under the 3.25 to 3.30% given in July. The headline sweep-cash figure hides the cause. Cash rose $7.1B only because long/short short credits rose $19.6B; without them it fell $12.5B in the quarter and is up 1.6% in a year while client assets grew 15%. Money-fund balances were flat and clients put cash into the market, so this is not 2023, but NIM now depends on old assets repricing, not on free cash growing.

I cut my five-year value 8%: Base EPS [[Base.eps]] at 16×, a multiple I now derive from a 9.5% cost of equity. The price fell further than the value, so the probability-weighted case returns [[pw_return]] and clears 13% at [[entry]]. The price asks for only [[Priced-in.cagr]] a year of EPS growth, against [[Base.cagr]] in my Base. The verb is probability-fragile: the break-even Bear odds are [[breakeven_bear]] against 25% assigned. December's cash balance excluding long/short settles it. The buyback fell to $0.5B at about $106 a share in the quarter, which keeps the Outsider grade at Steward.

tests.claim: That cash holds without the long/short balances.
tests.test: transactional sweep cash less long/short short credits (Q3: $429.5B; June: $442.0B) stays at or above $415B at December 31 (Jan 21 release) and in the October and November monthly reports.
tests.if_fail: move 10 points from Base to Bear (PW EV [[test1.pw_ev]], [[test1.pw_return]]/yr) → **[[test1.verb]]**, entry falls to [[test1.entry]].

tests.claim: That NIM reaches the guided exit rate on stable funding costs.
tests.test: Q4 NIM at or above 3.15% in the Jan 21 release, and a January Winter Business Update that guides 2027 revenue growth to at least +8% (the low end of the high-single-digit framework) with positive operating leverage.
tests.if_fail: Base FY2031 EPS cut to ≈$9.00, NIM stuck near 3.1% (PW EV [[test2.pw_ev]], [[test2.pw_return]]/yr) → **[[test2.verb]]**, entry [[test2.entry]].

tests.claim: That asset gathering and capital return both hold.
tests.test: Q4 core net new assets at or above a 5% annualized rate (≈$165B) with Advisor Services at or above 5% after the September long/short curbs, and a Q4 buyback of at least $1.0B with adjusted Tier 1 leverage at or below 7.0% (Jan 21 release).
tests.if_fail: move 10 points from Bull to Bear (PW EV [[test3.pw_ev]], [[test3.pw_return]]/yr) → **[[test3.verb]]**; the Outsider grade stays Steward and a second weak quarter moves it to Anti-Outsider.

return_math.epv: $68 a share on 2026's earnings held flat ($11.2B ÷ 9.5% ÷ 1.73B), $44 on five-year average earnings (FY2022–26E). Growth pays for 24% of today's price on the first measure and 51% on the second. The Bear ([[Bear.value]]) sits at the first because it keeps earnings roughly flat at 12×.
return_math.base_rate: Revenue of $28B puts Schwab in the >$25B bucket, where 31.8% of companies grew sales at least 5% a year in real terms over five years and the median is 2.0% ([`compounding.md`](../../frameworks/compounding.md)). The Bull's 8.4% nominal (about 5.9% real) is plausible. The Base's 6.3% nominal (about 3.8% real) sits above the median, carried by asset-linked fees that compound with markets and 5%+ organic gathering; it is the part I would trim first if the cash test fails. Tiers: Bull plausible, Base probable, Bear probable.
return_math.year_ten: Still growing: client assets compound on 5%+ organic gathering plus market returns without needing retained capital, and 16× is a mature-financial multiple, so the terminal multiple is not doing the work.
return_math.rr_note: The ratio is flattered by a Bull worth 2.6× spot; the Bear sits only 22% below spot because I value it near current earnings power.
